heroHeadline: Gotion Gnascent Na-Ion Hits 261 Wh/kg — Golden Lithium Awards Crown CATL and BYD's Next-Gen Batteries
heroSubtitle: Volkswagen-backed Gotion High-Tech launched its 'Gnascent' sodium-ion brand on May 17 at the 15th Global Technology Conference, unveiling a 261 Wh/kg high-energy cell (closing the gap with lower-tier NMC) and a 20,000-cycle grid-storage variant — both targeting mass production Q4 2026 and representing the first Western-accessible sodium-ion supply chain at scale outside CATL. China's inaugural Golden Lithium Awards (May 16, Shenzhen) recognized CATL's Qilin 3 ultra-fast charging, sodium-ion progress, and CTC 2.0 chassis integration, alongside BYD's Blade 2.0 and Hohan solid-state prototype at 400+ Wh/kg. CATL's separately announced Qilin 3 (April 21 Tech Day) demonstrated 10C continuous charging (3,000 kW output), targeting 1,000+ km range in 2027 production vehicles. German discount chain Lidl brought residential battery storage to the mass market on May 19, launching a €299 2.24 kWh LFP system compatible with Germany's 2M+ balcony solar installations — at €134/kWh, the lowest accessible price for European homeowners. The sodium-ion technology wave is now confirmed: two independent supply chains (CATL, Gotion) targeting commercial production in 2026 at performance levels viable for mainstream EVs.
footerNote: Data sourced from official company reports, IEA, BloombergNEF, Benchmark Mineral Intelligence, SNE Research, pv magazine, and peer-reviewed publications. Lab results distinguished from commercial production figures throughout.
